reason: Wording: vangoghletters.org letter 638 English translation reads verbatim “Just as we take the train to go to Tarascon or Rouen, we take death to go to a star.” It opens a paragraph, so the capital is the edition’s own; the French is “Tout comme nous prenons le train pour aller à Tarascon ou Rouen, nous prenons la mort pour aller à une étoile.” Date and place (Arles, 9 or 10 July 1888) and addressee (Theo) match the edition. Translator: the edition’s credits page names Sue Dyson and Imogen Forster as translators of the French letters, so the joint credit is right. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Van Gogh at 2 of 3 (months 5 and 10), not banned; this would be his third and last. In scope, a letter, publishable, a consoling mortality line. Source 115 characters, leads with the name, no dash. Tag Correspondence fits. One error in the evidence only: the sentence falls on folio 2v, not 1v (the edition marks [2v] immediately before it); the source line carries no folio, so the card is unaffected, but the evidence locator should read 2v.
